Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

Bloomberry Resorts Corporation

A hold-flattered but genuinely cleaner quarter. Consolidated EBITDA rose 64% YoY to P3.15bn (~$49m) on a 22.9% margin (+770bps), but P350m (~$5.5m) of that is VIP hold running at 3.37% against the 2.85% the company itself calls normal; hold-normalised EBITDA was +32% in Q3 and -5% over nine months, mass-table GGR fell 8%, and visitation dropped 4-9% at both Solaire properties. The P77bn (~$1.21bn) net-debt stack at ~6x annualised EBITDA (our estimate), with the P72bn facility's amortisation tripling from year three, remains the thesis constraint — the shares fell 4.8% to P1.79 on a day the PSEi hit a six-year low.

CAIXA Loterias S.A.

A record but visibly decelerating nine months: federal lottery sales of R$18.71bn (~$3.24bn), +3.9% YoY, with Q3 up only +1.3% to R$6.51bn (~$1.13bn) as the July-2025 average ticket repricing (+21.7%) lapped — nominal growth is now below any plausible inflation print, the operating-cost ratio rose 240bps to 21.1% of sales, and the retail network shrank again. A volume-led quarter from an unlisted B2B supplier that discloses growth rates, not money: sportsbook GGR +33.4% YoY on actives +82.7% and bets +31.9% means GGR per active fell ~27% (our arithmetic) — breadth from new operator go-lives and World Cup/Esports World Cup casuals, not deeper monetisation. Growth has decelerated from +61% in Q1 and +42.7% in H1 but re-accelerated versus an implied ~+24% Q2 (est.), while lapping a soft-hold September 2025 comp. With no revenue, EBITDA, handle, hold, partner-count or concentration disclosure, this is a momentum signal, not an underwritable result.

BetMakers Technology Group

A clean quarter on the metrics that matter for a B2B supplier: record Adj. EBITDA of A$5.9m (~$4.1m) at a 23.8% margin on revenue of A$24.7m (~$17.4m), +16.3% YoY in constant currency (+11.8% reported), with opex down 2.4% YoY and the 70% gross-margin / 25% EBITDA-margin long-term goals now one quarter away. But the equity is a merger-arb instrument, not a growth stock: Tabcorp's A$0.24 cash scheme caps the upside, the shares sit ~12% below the offer at A$0.21, and the beat mostly sharpens the question of whether the board recommended a sale at the bottom of the margin curve.

A weak core quarter wrapped around a transformational deal. Q3-26 revenue fell 12% YoY to €8.5m (~$9.5m) — the third consecutive YoY decline, now accelerating — and adj. A clean, high-quality half: revenue +28.2% reported / +20.8% constant currency to $3,823m, underlying EBITDA +32.8% to $1,921m with a record 50.4% Q2 margin despite a c.2–2.5pp fuel headwind, pre-exceptional EPS +41% to 11.7c and leverage down to 1.6x (0.5x lease-adjusted). Market report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

United States

Q3 2026 is the quarter the regulated US online market stopped being a growth story and became a share-and-margin story: iGaming growth slowed to a record-low 12% YoY (Citizens; ~13-14% on summed state monthlies) with no new states since Rhode Island, and sportsbook handle was flat-to-down outside the June–July World Cup window while CFTC-regulated prediction markets printed >$82bn of September volume paying zero state gaming tax. For an entrant the addressable regulated pool is large (~$6.5–6.8bn/month commercial GGR, ~$1.0bn/month iGaming) but closed-access, high-tax, top-two dominated and now contested by an untaxed federal channel.

~$3.06bnUS iGaming GGR, Q3-26 (7 states, sum of monthlies)+~13.6% est. (Citizens: +12%, lowest on record vs 16% in Q1/Q2)
$1.00bnSports betting GGR, Aug-26 (AGA)-15.6% YoY; hold 9.2% vs 10.8%
$11.60bnSports betting handle, Jul-26 (AGA)+31.9% YoY (World Cup); Aug $10.89bn -0.7%

Macau

Macau's 9M-2026 casino GGR of MOP187.12bn (~$23.19bn, +3.2% YoY) flatters a market that has rolled over: four straight monthly year-on-year declines through September (five through October), a Q3 of MOP60.22bn (~$7.46bn, -3.8%) driven by a 7.9% fall in mass/premium-mass baccarat, and GGR per visitor down ~5% even as arrivals rose 8.5%. The regime is stable but closed — six concessions locked to 31 Dec 2032, a 40% effective levy on GGR, zero licensed online — so for B2Tech the only realistic exposure is B2B supply into the one product line still growing, slots (+~19% YoY).

Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

South Africa

South Africa is now a R84.5bn (~$5.1bn) GGR market whose growth is entirely online bookmaking: betting is 70% of GGR, ~86% of it online, and the land-based estate is shrinking. The rules are moving against the online channel — a proposed 20% national tax on online GGR (decision Feb 2027), new advertising norms, and an NGB site-blocking programme — while interactive casino remains illegal and licensing stays provincial. For B2Tech the prize is real but the licence-to-tax arbitrage that built the market is closing.
